In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) subsystems are a good way to reuse hardware and software modules in the design of SoCs; 2) the audio subsystem is a good example of a subsystem that can be reused across SoCs; 3) there are many challenges to be overcome to make the subsystems paradigm a viable solution; 4) the challenges are mostly in the software area and in the area of integration of subsystems into a SoC.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are exploring how to make the design of subsystems and SoCs more predictable and more efficient.
we have demonstrated that subsystem-based SoC integration offers a viable solution for reducing cost and time-to market in SoC design while retaining low-power, high-performance processing.
the use of subsystems for SoC integration can be a viable approach for the design of future SoCs, especially when the subsystems are designed with the SoC integration in mind.
The main takeaway from our work is that
subsystems can be a viable alternative to SoCs in terms of performance, power and area, while reducing time-to-market and development cost.
the subsystem-based SoC design methodology is an attractive alternative to traditional SoC integration approaches.
subsystems can be a powerful paradigm for efficient SoCs.
